C"],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2022,5]]},"abstract":"<jats:title>Abstract<\/jats:title>\n                  <jats:p>Wormholes are intriguing classical solutions in General Relativity, that have fascinated theoretical physicists for decades. In recent years, especially in Holography, gravitational Wormhole geometries have found a new life in many theoretical ideas related to quantum aspects of gravity. These ideas primarily revolve around aspects of quantum entanglement and quantum information in (semi-classical) gravity. This is an introductory and pedagogical review of Wormholes and their recent applications in Gauge-Gravity duality and related ideas.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1140\/epjc\/s10052-022-10376-z","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2022,5,16]],"date-time":"2022-05-16T07:05:58Z","timestamp":1652684758000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1007\/springer_crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":45,"title":["Wormholes and holography: an introduction"],"prefix":"10.1140","volume":"82","author":[{"given":"Arnab","family":"Kundu","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"297","published-online":{"date-parts":[[2022,5,16]]},"reference":[{"key":"10376_CR1","unstructured":"Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration, First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results.
